registry: The Tank Guide University Research Library

verification_status.verified: Source located at its official location; citation metadata as registered is correct and the content supports the use described in verification_note.
verification_status.verified_with_metadata_correction: Source located and content verified, but registered citation metadata (title, author, publisher, year, DOI, or canonical URL) required correction.
verification_status.verified_limited_scope: Source located and verified, but it supports only a narrower scope than the package use implies.
verification_status.broken_or_moved: Registered URL no longer resolves to the cited source and no verified replacement location has been recorded.
verification_status.citation_problem: Citation metadata could not be reconciled with the source located (wrong title, author, or document).
verification_status.unable_to_verify: Source could not be located or checked during verification.
verification_status.unverified_citation_from_package: Pre-verification status: citation metadata recorded as given in the package and not yet checked against the live source. No longer assigned to any Summer Heat pilot record; assigned to PKG-2026-08-gh-kh-ph source records at registration (extraction stage).

evidence_role.reference_data: Source of specific numeric values or relationships used by the package.
evidence_role.applied_guidance: Extension/aquaculture applied guidance; context differs from home aquariums.
evidence_role.preparedness_and_safety_guidance: General emergency-preparedness or safety guidance; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.preparedness_context: Contextual background for severe-weather preparedness; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.analogous_guidance_limited_scope: Non-aquarium guidance used only for a narrowly stated principle.
evidence_role.manufacturer_product_documentation: Vendor documentation of its own product features. Not independent scientific evidence.
evidence_role.veterinary_clinical_guidance: Veterinary reference or proceedings giving clinical/husbandry guidance.
evidence_role.hobby_publication_context: Aquarium trade, hobby publication or retailer material cited for practical context; not independent scientific evidence.
evidence_role.hobbyist_discussion_not_evidence: Hobbyist forum or community material the package used to identify recurring questions and practices, explicitly not as scientific evidence.

source_origin.original_package_citation: Cited in the original research package's bibliography (carries an original_package_key such as S1–S16).
source_origin.supplementary_verification_source: Added later during an independent verification pass to support a claim whose original citation was mismatched. Not an original package citation; carries no original_package_key.

vocabularies.original_package_key: Object recording how the source is identified in its package. Summer Heat: key is the package's S# number. PKG-2026-08-gh-kh-ph: the package has no source numbering, so key is the bibliography entry's own author–year (or organization + title) label (key_type 'bibliography_entry_label'), with bibliography_tier, bibliography_tier_position and bibliography_entry_verbatim preserved.
vocabularies.verified_bibliographic_fields: Optional fields added when a source is independently verified: authors (ordered list of full names as published), journal, volume, issue, article_number, page_range, publication_date (ISO date; publication_date_role qualifies it when it is not the issue date), book_series, book_title, editors, publisher. metadata_correction (object) records a substantive citation correction: correction_type, the original package values, the corrected values and a note. The original package citation is never rewritten; it stays in original_package_key.

sources.title: Dissolved organic carbon from the upper Rio Negro protects zebrafish (Danio rerio) against ionoregulatory disturbances caused by low pH exposure
sources.author_or_organization: Duarte, Rafael M.; Smith, D. Scott; Val, Adalberto L.; Wood, Chris M.

The study found that upper Rio Negro dissolved organic carbon provided near-complete protection against ionoregulatory disturbances in zebrafish exposed acutely to pH 4.0 in ion-poor water, including reduced Na+ and Cl− losses and stimulation of Na+ uptake.
